learning_outcomes.text: Identify opportunities for innovative data-oriented applications in continuously evolving technological environments.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its organization and management, different business sectors, and entrepreneurship opportunities, with the aim of facilitating solutions from data science and engineering.
Propose solutions and business plans based on data exploitation and communicate these proposals adequately.
Know the concept of a company and its typology.
Know the institutional framework of the company.
Know the legal framework of the company.
Know the organization of the company.
Know the management mechanisms of the company.

syllabus_topics: Functioning of economic activity and types of markets
Concept and objectives of the company
Types of company: economic, organizational, and legal criteria
Asset and results analysis for decision making
Valuation of investment and financing projects
Management levels and functions of management
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as EX.ORD + P1 + P2 + P3 + P. To pass, a minimum of 40% (2.4 points) is required in the final exam (EX.ORD) and a minimum of 40% (1.6 points) in the sum of P1, P2, P3, and P. The overall final grade must be at least 5 points. If the final grade exceeds 5 points but a minimum is not met, the final grade will be 4.5. For extraordinary calls, an EX.EXTR exam (max 6 points, min 2.4 to pass) and/or an EX.PR exam (max 4 points, min 1.6 to pass) can be taken to cover failed sections.
